bibliography.title: References
bibliography.bibliomixed: 1W. Zhang, K. Zhao, T. Zhou, X. Feng, D. Niyato, S. Zheng, and Y. Chen. A Survey of Quantum Transformers: Architectures, Challenges and Outlooks. arXiv:2504.03192 (2025). Adversarially verified (3-0).

2G. Li, X. Zhao, and X. Wang. Quantum Self-Attention Neural Networks for Text Classification. Science China Information Sciences (2024), DOI 10.1007/s11432-023-3879-7; arXiv:2205.05625 (2022). Adversarially verified (3-0). Representative of a broader confirmed line: QASA (arXiv:2504.05336), QNN-SAM (Neurocomputing 2026), QPSAN (arXiv:2605.25365).

3F. Meyer and M. Lewis. Modelling Lexical Ambiguity with Density Matrices. Proceedings of CoNLL 2020; arXiv:2010.05670. Adversarially verified (3-0). Correction to the source report: the density-matrix word embeddings are learned by classical NEURAL models, not variational quantum circuits, and the authors are Meyer & Lewis (not "Meyer & Sadrzadeh").

4E. Miles Stoudenmire and David J. Schwab. Supervised Learning with Quantum-Inspired Tensor Networks. Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 29 (2016); arXiv:1605.05775. Adversarially verified (3-0).

5Zhao-Yu Han, Jun Wang, Heng Fan, Lei Wang, and Pan Zhang. Unsupervised Generative Modeling Using Matrix Product States. Physical Review X 8, 031012 (2018), DOI 10.1103/PhysRevX.8.031012; arXiv:1709.01662. Adversarially verified (3-0).

6Paola Zizzi. From Quantum Metalanguage to the Logic of Qubits. arXiv:1003.5976 (2010); and Paola Zizzi, Basic Logic and Quantum Entanglement, arXiv:quant-ph/0611119 (2006). Adversarially verified (3-0) for the quantum-metalanguage / logic-of-qubits and Basic-logic–no-cloning/no-deleting claims. The specifically "paranormal" (paraconsistent AND paracomplete) quantum-logic framing with amplitude-valued assertion degrees is the report author's synthesis and was not separately confirmed.
7Newton C. A. da Costa and Décio Krause. Schrödinger Logics. Studia Logica 53(4):533–550 (1994), DOI 10.1007/BF01057649. Adversarially verified (3-0).

8Wilfrid Hodges. Tarski's Truth Definitions. Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, plato.stanford.edu/entries/tarski-truth/. Located in search (authoritative secondary reference); not adversarially re-verified.

9Seth Lloyd, Masoud Mohseni, and Patrick Rebentrost. Quantum Principal Component Analysis. Nature Physics 10, 631–633 (2014), DOI 10.1038/nphys3029; arXiv:1307.0401. Located in search (primary, canonical); not adversarially re-verified.

10John Preskill. Quantum Computing in the NISQ Era and Beyond. Quantum 2, 79 (2018), DOI 10.22331/q-2018-08-06-79; arXiv:1801.00862. Located in search (primary, canonical); not adversarially re-verified.

11El Amine Cherrat, Iordanis Kerenidis, et al. (QASA) — S.-Y. Chen and colleagues. Quantum Adaptive Self-Attention for Quantum Transformer Models. arXiv:2504.05336 (2025). Adversarially verified (3-0) as an instance of hybrid quantum-transformer / density-operator attention. NOTE: the authors attribute observed gains to a low-rank bottleneck, "not to quantumness."

12Jun Tang, Yuehaw Khoo, and Lexing Ying. Initialization and Training of Matrix Product State Probabilistic Models. arXiv:2505.06419 (2025). Adversarially verified (3-0): identifies the "causality trap" of randomly-initialized MPS Born machines and a warm-start remedy.

13Ivan Glasser, Ryan Sweke, Nicola Pancotti, Jens Eisert, and J. Ignacio Cirac. Expressive Power of Tensor-Network Factorizations for Probabilistic Modeling. Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 32 (2019); arXiv:1907.03741. Adversarially verified (3-0): tensor-network / probabilistic-graphical-model correspondence (non-negative MPS ↔ hidden Markov models), with unbounded expressive-power separations.

14Tensor Network based Gene Regulatory Network Inference for Single-Cell Transcriptomic Data. arXiv:2509.06891 (2025). Located in search (primary; quantum-inspired tensor-network method for single-cell GRN inference); not adversarially re-verified.

15Steven French and Décio Krause. Identity in Physics: A Historical, Philosophical, and Formal Analysis. Oxford University Press (2006). Consistent extension of the verified da Costa & Krause (1994) anchor; the book itself was not separately adjudicated in this pass.

16Jarrod R. McClean, Sergio Boixo, Vadim N. Smelyanskiy, Ryan Babbush, and Hartmut Neven. Barren Plateaus in Quantum Neural Network Training Landscapes. Nature Communications 9, 4812 (2018), DOI 10.1038/s41467-018-07090-4; arXiv:1803.11173. Located in search (primary, canonical); not adversarially re-verified.
